title: The Gupta Era: An Age of Tireless Creativity

learn.hook: A king who played the veena on his coins and a court poet who carved his praises on Ashoka's pillar: welcome to the Gupta age!
points: The Gupta dynasty became powerful in the early 4th century CE. Chandragupta I, who married the Licchavi princess Kumāradevī, made the kingdom strong around 320 CE.

His son Samudragupta won many wars. His court poet Hariṣheṇa composed a praśasti (praise poem) that was carved on the Ashokan pillar at Prayāgarāja (Prayagraj). Some of his gold coins show him playing the veena.
Chandragupta II (also called Vikramāditya) defeated the Shakas of western India. The Chinese Buddhist pilgrim Faxian (Fa-hien) travelled in India during his reign.
Kumāragupta I is linked with the founding of the great university at Nālandā. Skandagupta defended the empire against the Hūṇas from Central Asia.
The Guptas issued many beautiful gold coins. Their rule is remembered as a time of great creativity in science, art and literature.

example.q: Samudragupta's achievements are known from a poem carved on an older Ashokan pillar. Why are such praśastis useful but also to be read carefully?
steps: A praśasti gives names of places, kings and wars of the time, which is valuable information.
But it was written by a court poet to praise the king.
So historians compare it with coins and other sources before accepting every claim.
example.answer: They are useful records, but as praise poems they may exaggerate, so they are checked against other evidence.

learn.reallife: The pillar with both Ashoka's edicts and Samudragupta's praśasti can be seen inside the Allahabad Fort in Prayagraj.

quiz.q: Around which year did Chandragupta I make the Gupta kingdom strong?
quiz.explain: The Gupta rise is dated to around 320 CE, in the 4th century CE.
steps: The Guptas became powerful in the early 4th century CE.
Chandragupta I made the kingdom strong around 320 CE.
320 BCE would be the Mauryan period, so the answer is 320 CE.
Answer: 320 CE
quiz.mistake: Confuses CE with BCE or with the Mauryan date

quiz.q: Who composed the praśasti of Samudragupta?
quiz.explain: Hariṣheṇa was Samudragupta's court poet.
steps: Samudragupta's praise poem (praśasti) was written by his court poet.
That poet was Hariṣheṇa.
Kālidāsa and Bāṇabhaṭṭa were other writers; Faxian was a pilgrim.
Answer: Hariṣheṇa

quiz.q: Samudragupta's praśasti was carved on:
quiz.explain: It was inscribed on the same pillar that carries Ashoka's edicts, now in Prayagraj.
steps: Hariṣheṇa's praśasti was carved on an older pillar.
It is the Ashokan pillar now at Prayāgarāja (Prayagraj).
It is not the Iron Pillar in Delhi.
Answer: An Ashokan pillar at Prayagraj
quiz.mistake: Mixes it up with the Iron Pillar

quiz.q: Some of Samudragupta's coins show him:
quiz.explain: These coins suggest he loved music as well as war.
steps: Some of Samudragupta's gold coins show him with a musical instrument.
He is shown playing the veena.
This suggests he loved music as well as war.
Answer: Playing the veena
quiz.mistake: Does not know about the famous veena coins

quiz.q: Chandragupta II is also known as:
quiz.explain: Chandragupta II took the title Vikramāditya.
steps: Chandragupta II defeated the Shakas of western India.
He took the title Vikramāditya.
Ashoka, Kanishka and Milinda were other kings.
Answer: Vikramāditya
quiz.mistake: Mixes up titles of different kings

quiz.q: Which Chinese pilgrim visited India during Chandragupta II's reign?
quiz.explain: Faxian came in the early 5th century. Xuanzang came later, in Harsha's time.
steps: A Chinese Buddhist pilgrim travelled in India during Chandragupta II's reign.
That pilgrim was Faxian (Fa-hien).
Xuanzang came later, in Harsha's time.
Answer: Faxian
quiz.mistake: Confuses Faxian with Xuanzang

quiz.q: The famous university at Nālandā is linked with which Gupta ruler?
quiz.explain: Nālandā is believed to have been founded in the 5th century under Kumāragupta I.
steps: The great university at Nālandā was founded in the Gupta age.
It is linked with Kumāragupta I.
Skandagupta is known for fighting the Hūṇas.
Answer: Kumāragupta I
quiz.mistake: Picks the more famous Gupta rulers

quiz.q: Skandagupta is remembered for defending the empire against the:
quiz.explain: The Hūṇas from Central Asia attacked in the 5th century; Skandagupta pushed them back.
steps: Skandagupta defended the Gupta Empire.
He fought the Hūṇas from Central Asia.
The Mughals and British came many centuries later.
Answer: Hūṇas
quiz.mistake: Mixes up invaders from different periods

teach.ask: Gappu wants to meet the Gupta kings. Tell him who the main rulers were and what they are known for.
teach.praise: Chandragupta I, Samudragupta, Chandragupta II and more, with golden coins. A royal family indeed!
teach.nudge: Good! Which king had a praise poem carved on a pillar, or played the veena on his coins?

revise.summary: The Guptas rose around 320 CE under Chandragupta I. Samudragupta's wars are praised in Hariṣheṇa's praśasti, Chandragupta II (Vikramāditya) defeated the Shakas, Kumāragupta I is linked with Nālandā, and Skandagupta fought the Hūṇas.

topics.title: Science and mathematics in the Gupta age

learn.hook: About 1,500 years ago, a 23-year-old Indian astronomer explained eclipses with shadows, not demons!
points: Āryabhaṭa wrote the Āryabhaṭīya in 499 CE. He stated that the Earth rotates on its axis, which makes the stars seem to move across the sky.
Āryabhaṭa explained that eclipses happen because of the shadows of the Earth and the Moon. He gave a very close value of pi (π), about 3.1416.
Varāhamihira wrote the Bṛihat Saṁhitā, a great book on astronomy, weather, plants, gems, building and much more.
Indian mathematicians used the decimal place-value system, which later spread to the world through Arab scholars.
Metal-workers made the Iron Pillar, now in Mehrauli, Delhi. More than 1,500 years later it has hardly rusted, showing their skill in metallurgy.

example.q: Āryabhaṭa said that the stars seem to move from east to west because the Earth rotates. How can you test this idea with a simple observation?
steps: Sit in a moving train and look at trees outside.
The trees seem to move backward, though it is the train that moves.
In the same way, the Earth's rotation makes the sky seem to turn around us.
example.answer: Like trees seeming to move past a moving train, the sky seems to move because the Earth itself rotates.

learn.reallife: India's first satellite, launched in 1975, was named Aryabhata in honour of the great astronomer.

games.title: Gupta science: true or false?
items: Āryabhaṭa wrote that the Earth rotates on its axis.
He explained the apparent movement of stars by the Earth's rotation.
Āryabhaṭa believed eclipses were caused by shadows.
He explained eclipses using the shadows of the Earth and the Moon.
The Iron Pillar in Delhi has rusted away completely.
It has hardly rusted even after more than 1,500 years.
India's first satellite was named after Varāhamihira.
It was named Aryabhata and launched in 1975.
Āryabhaṭa's value of pi was about 3.1416.
His value was remarkably close to the modern value.

quiz.q: Which book did Āryabhaṭa write in 499 CE?
quiz.explain: The Āryabhaṭīya covers mathematics and astronomy.
steps: Āryabhaṭa wrote his book in 499 CE.
It is the Āryabhaṭīya, on mathematics and astronomy.
The Bṛihat Saṁhitā was written by Varāhamihira.
Answer: Āryabhaṭīya
quiz.mistake: Mixes up Āryabhaṭa's book with Varāhamihira's

quiz.q: According to Āryabhaṭa, why do the stars seem to move across the night sky?
options: The stars are pulled by the Moon
The Earth rotates on its axis
The sky is a rotating dome
quiz.explain: He realised it is the Earth turning that makes the stars appear to move.
steps: Āryabhaṭa stated that the Earth rotates on its axis.
This turning makes the stars seem to move across the sky.
Like trees seeming to move past a moving train.
Answer: The Earth rotates on its axis
quiz.mistake: Trusts appearances over reasoning

quiz.q: How did Āryabhaṭa explain eclipses?
options: By a demon swallowing the Sun
By the shadows of the Earth and the Moon
quiz.explain: A solar eclipse is the Moon's shadow on Earth; a lunar eclipse is Earth's shadow on the Moon.
steps: Āryabhaṭa used shadows to explain eclipses.
Solar eclipse: the Moon's shadow on Earth; lunar eclipse: Earth's shadow on the Moon.
So eclipses are caused by the shadows of the Earth and the Moon.
Answer: By the shadows of the Earth and the Moon
quiz.mistake: Accepts old myths instead of the scientific explanation

quiz.q: Āryabhaṭa's value of pi was about:
quiz.explain: His value, about 3.1416, is very close to the modern value of pi.
steps: Āryabhaṭa gave a very close value of pi.
His value was about 3.1416.
That is very close to the modern value of pi.
Answer: 3.1416
quiz.mistake: Rounds pi to 3

quiz.q: Who wrote the Bṛihat Saṁhitā?
quiz.explain: Varāhamihira's Bṛihat Saṁhitā covers astronomy, weather, plants, gems and more.
steps: The Bṛihat Saṁhitā is a great book on astronomy, weather, plants, gems and building.
It was written by Varāhamihira.
Āryabhaṭa wrote the Āryabhaṭīya.
Answer: Varāhamihira
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the two astronomers

quiz.q: Why is the Iron Pillar in Delhi famous?
options: It has hardly rusted for more than 1,500 years
It is the tallest tower in India
quiz.explain: Its rust resistance shows the great skill of ancient Indian iron-workers.
steps: The Iron Pillar is more than 1,500 years old.
Yet it has hardly rusted.
This shows the great skill of ancient Indian metal-workers.
Answer: It has hardly rusted for more than 1,500 years
quiz.mistake: Does not know what is special about the pillar

quiz.q: The Iron Pillar stands today in:
quiz.explain: It stands in the Qutb complex at Mehrauli, Delhi.
steps: The Iron Pillar was made by Gupta-age metal-workers.
Today it stands in Mehrauli, Delhi (in the Qutb complex).
So the answer is Mehrauli, Delhi.
Answer: Mehrauli, Delhi
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the location with other ancient sites

quiz.q: In which year was India's first satellite, Aryabhata, launched?
quiz.explain: The satellite Aryabhata was launched in 1975.
steps: India named its first satellite after Āryabhaṭa.
The satellite Aryabhata was launched in 1975.
So the year is 1975.
Answer: 1975
quiz.mistake: Guesses a different famous year

teach.ask: Gappu wants to know what Gupta-age scientists discovered. Tell him!
teach.praise: The Earth spins, eclipses are shadows, and iron that does not rust. Brilliant!
teach.nudge: Nice! But what did Āryabhaṭa say about eclipses, or about the Earth spinning?

revise.summary: Āryabhaṭa's Āryabhaṭīya (499 CE) said the Earth rotates, explained eclipses by shadows and gave pi as about 3.1416. Varāhamihira wrote the Bṛihat Saṁhitā, Indians used decimal place value, and the Iron Pillar shows great metal skill.
focus: Know Āryabhaṭa's ideas on rotation, eclipses and pi
Know Varāhamihira and the Bṛihat Saṁhitā
Know the spread of decimal place value
Know why the Iron Pillar is special
remember: Āryabhaṭīya, 499 CE: the Earth rotates on its axis
Eclipses are caused by the shadows of the Earth and the Moon; pi ≈ 3.1416
Iron Pillar (Mehrauli, Delhi) has hardly rusted in 1,500+ years
traps: Don't mix up the Āryabhaṭīya with the Bṛihat Saṁhitā
Don't say the stars move across the sky; they only seem to move because the Earth turns
Eclipses are explained by shadows, not myths

topics.title: Art and literature of the Gupta age

learn.hook: A cloud carrying a love message across India, and cave walls glowing with paintings: Gupta-age art still amazes the world.
points: Kālidāsa was a great Sanskrit poet and playwright. His works include the play Abhijñāna-Shākuntalam and the poem Meghadūta, in which a cloud carries a message.
Many of the famous paintings in the Ajanta caves in Maharashtra were made in the 5th century CE. They show scenes from the Buddha's life and stories (Jātakas) with rich colours.
Some of the earliest stone temples were built in this age, such as the Dashāvatāra temple at Deogarh in Uttar Pradesh. The Udayagiri caves near Vidisha have a huge carving of Varāha.
Nālandā grew into a great centre of learning where students studied many subjects.
Sanskrit became a major language of literature, learning and royal inscriptions.

example.q: In the Meghadūta, a cloud flies over mountains, rivers and towns to carry a message. What can a historian learn from such a poem?
steps: The poem names and describes places, rivers and mountains along the route.
So it shows what people of that time knew about India's geography.
It also shows the beauty of Sanskrit poetry of that age.
example.answer: It shows the geography people knew and the high skill of Sanskrit poetry at that time.

learn.reallife: Ajanta's caves near Aurangabad (Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar) are a UNESCO World Heritage Site, visited by people from all over the world.

items.text: In the Meghadūta, a ___ carries a message.

quiz.q: Who wrote Abhijñāna-Shākuntalam?
quiz.explain: Kālidāsa wrote this famous Sanskrit play.
steps: Abhijñāna-Shākuntalam is a famous Sanskrit play.
It was written by Kālidāsa, the great poet and playwright.
Āryabhaṭa was an astronomer; Tulsidas lived much later.
Answer: Kālidāsa
quiz.mistake: Mixes up poets of different periods

quiz.q: In Kālidāsa's Meghadūta, who carries the message?
quiz.explain: Megha means cloud and dūta means messenger.
steps: Break the title: megha = cloud, dūta = messenger.
In the poem, a cloud flies over mountains and rivers carrying a message.
So a cloud carries the message.
Answer: A cloud
quiz.mistake: Guesses without breaking the title into parts

quiz.q: The Ajanta caves are famous mainly for their:
quiz.explain: Ajanta's paintings show the Buddha's life and Jātaka stories.
steps: The Ajanta caves have paintings from the 5th century CE.
They show the Buddha's life and Jātaka stories in rich colours.
So they are famous for their wall paintings.
Answer: Wall paintings
quiz.mistake: Mixes up Ajanta with other monuments

quiz.q: In which state are the Ajanta caves?
quiz.explain: Ajanta is in Maharashtra.
steps: The Ajanta caves are in western India.
They are in the state of Maharashtra.
So the answer is Maharashtra.
Answer: Maharashtra
quiz.mistake: Confuses Ajanta with other cave sites

quiz.q: The Dashāvatāra temple, one of the early stone temples, is at:
quiz.explain: The Dashāvatāra temple at Deogarh in Uttar Pradesh is from the Gupta age.
steps: Some of the earliest stone temples were built in the Gupta age.
One is the Dashāvatāra temple at Deogarh in Uttar Pradesh.
Thanjavur, Khajuraho and Konark temples are from later periods.
Answer: Deogarh
quiz.mistake: Picks famous temples from later periods

quiz.q: Which language was most used for literature and royal inscriptions in the Gupta age?
quiz.explain: Sanskrit flourished as a language of literature and inscriptions.
steps: In the Gupta age, Sanskrit was used for literature, learning and royal inscriptions.
English, Persian and Urdu came into use much later.
So the language was Sanskrit.
Answer: Sanskrit
quiz.mistake: Picks a language from a later period

quiz.q: Many Ajanta paintings were made in which century?
quiz.explain: Many of Ajanta's best-known paintings date to the 5th century CE.
steps: Ajanta's famous paintings were made in the Gupta age.
That is the 5th century CE.
5th century BCE would be far too early.
Answer: 5th century CE
quiz.mistake: Mixes up CE and BCE

quiz.q: What are Jātaka stories?
options: Stories of the Buddha's earlier lives
quiz.explain: Jātakas tell of the Buddha's past lives and teach good values.
steps: Ajanta paintings show the Buddha's life and Jātaka stories.
Jātakas are stories of the Buddha's earlier lives.
They teach good values.
Answer: Stories of the Buddha's earlier lives
quiz.mistake: Does not know what Jātakas are

teach.ask: Gappu loves stories and pictures. Tell him about the art and literature of the Gupta age.
teach.praise: Kālidāsa's poems, Ajanta's paintings and early temples. That's tireless creativity!
teach.nudge: Good! Who was the famous poet, and where are the painted caves?

revise.summary: The Gupta age was rich in art and literature: Kālidāsa wrote Abhijñāna-Shākuntalam and Meghadūta, the Ajanta caves were painted in the 5th century CE, early stone temples like Deogarh were built, and Sanskrit flourished.
focus: Know the Ajanta paintings, their place and their themes
Know early stone temples and cave carvings
Know Nālandā and the role of Sanskrit
remember: Ajanta (Maharashtra): 5th-century CE paintings of the Buddha's life and Jātakas
Dashāvatāra temple, Deogarh (UP); Varāha carving at Udayagiri near Vidisha
Jātakas = stories of the Buddha's earlier lives
traps: Ajanta is famous for paintings, not iron pillars or coins
Ajanta paintings are 5th century CE, not BCE
